title: Diabetes Emergency Card

warningSymptoms.symptom: Excessive thirst and dry mouth
Frequent urination
Blurred or double vision
Nausea or vomiting that will not stop
Fruity or acetone smell on breath
Confusion, difficulty speaking, or disorientation
Rapid deep breathing (Kussmaul breathing)
Loss of consciousness or seizure

immediateActions.action: Check blood sugar if a glucometer is available. Note the reading.
If blood sugar is below 4 mmol/L (70 mg/dL), give the person a sugary drink or glucose tablets immediately.
If blood sugar is above 20 mmol/L (360 mg/dL) or you see critical symptoms, call emergency services or go to the nearest hospital.
Keep the person sitting upright. Give small sips of water if they are conscious.
Bring all current medications and the glucometer reading to the hospital.

whenToGoToER: Blood sugar reading above 20 mmol/L (360 mg/dL) that does not come down
Blood sugar reading below 3 mmol/L (54 mg/dL) that does not respond to sugar intake
The person is unconscious or having a seizure
Persistent vomiting for more than 2 hours
Fruity breath smell combined with rapid breathing
doNotDo: Do not give insulin if you suspect low blood sugar (hypoglycaemia)
Do not give food or drink to someone who is unconscious or having a seizure
Do not assume the person is drunk. Diabetic emergencies can mimic alcohol intoxication
Do not delay going to the hospital while waiting for blood sugar to normalise

title: Hypertension Emergency Card

warningSymptoms.symptom: Severe headache that comes on suddenly
Nosebleed that will not stop
Blurred vision or seeing spots
Dizziness or feeling faint
Chest pain or tightness
Difficulty breathing or shortness of breath
Sudden difficulty speaking or understanding speech
Sudden weakness or numbness on one side of the body

immediateActions.action: Have the person sit or lie down in a comfortable position immediately.
Loosen any tight clothing around the neck and chest.
If a blood pressure monitor is available, take a reading. Note the numbers.
If blood pressure is above 180/120 mmHg or any critical symptoms are present, call emergency services immediately.
Do not give extra blood pressure medication unless specifically instructed by a doctor for emergencies.

whenToGoToER: Chest pain or tightness that lasts more than 5 minutes
Sudden severe headache unlike any headache before
Sudden difficulty speaking, seeing, or moving one side of the body (possible stroke)
Difficulty breathing that does not improve with rest
Nosebleed that does not stop after 20 minutes of pressure
doNotDo: Do not take extra doses of blood pressure medication without medical guidance
Do not drive yourself to the hospital if you feel faint or dizzy
Do not ignore a sudden severe headache, even if blood pressure seems normal
Do not wait to see if stroke symptoms go away on their own. Every minute matters

title: General Health Emergency Card

warningSymptoms.symptom: Sudden high fever above 39 degrees C (102 degrees F)
Persistent vomiting or diarrhoea for more than 6 hours
Severe allergic reaction with swelling of face or throat
Difficulty breathing or wheezing that gets worse
Sudden severe pain in the chest, abdomen, or head
Uncontrolled bleeding from any wound

immediateActions.action: Stay calm. Assess whether the person is conscious and breathing.
If the person is unconscious but breathing, place them on their side in the recovery position.
Call emergency services or arrange transport to the nearest hospital.
If there is bleeding, apply firm pressure with a clean cloth.
Gather all current medications and any relevant medical documents to bring to the hospital.

whenToGoToER: Loss of consciousness for any duration
Difficulty breathing that does not improve
Severe allergic reaction with throat or face swelling
Uncontrolled bleeding that soaks through bandages
Severe chest pain or abdominal pain
Any injury from a fall, especially for elderly patients
doNotDo: Do not move someone who may have a spinal injury from a fall
Do not give food or water to someone who is vomiting or unconscious
Do not apply a tourniquet to stop bleeding unless you are trained to do so
Do not delay calling for help while searching for information online
